name: SAFFiR
maker: Virginia Tech with the US Naval Research Laboratory
def: Bipedal firefighting robot developed for the US Navy that walked a decommissioned ship's compartments and aimed a hose at a live fire.
body: SAFFiR is 1.78 m tall and weighs about 65 kg, with legs driven by linear series elastic actuators and whole body momentum control so it can stay upright on a moving deck and step over door sills. It navigates smoke using infrared stereo vision and a rotating laser scanner, with a human supervisor able to take over any task. In November 2014 the Office of Naval Research tested it aboard the ex-USS Shadwell, where it walked uneven flooring, located overheated equipment by thermal imaging and suppressed a fire with a hose.
facts: Fought a live fire aboard the ex-USS Shadwell in November 2014
Funded by the Office of Naval Research with the Naval Research Laboratory
specs: Linear series elastic actuators with titanium springs
Infrared stereo vision, rotating lidar, six axis force and torque sensors in the ankles
Semi autonomous task execution with a human supervisor in the loop
